name: Stripe
description: Stripe describes itself as "financial infrastructure to grow your revenue," letting businesses accept payments, offer financial services, and implement custom revenue models — from your first transaction to your billionth.
best_for: Stripe states it serves enterprises (including half of Fortune 100 companies), startups, SaaS platforms, marketplaces, ecommerce businesses, and AI companies building payment or billing flows.
features: Subscription and billing management (200M+ active subscriptions on Stripe Billing)
Agentic Commerce Protocol for AI-driven purchases

alternatives.name: Plaid
alternatives.description: Connects applications to bank accounts and financial data, often used alongside payment processors to verify accounts or pull transaction data.
alternatives.best_for: Companies building fintech products that need to verify bank accounts or access financial data.

alternatives.name: Twilio
alternatives.description: A broader developer API platform for communications (SMS, voice, email) rather than payments.
alternatives.best_for: Companies needing customer communications (e.g., payment confirmations, fraud alerts) alongside a payments stack.

pricing.starting_price: 2.9% + $0.30 per successful domestic-card transaction on Stripe’s US standard pricing page

tiers.name: Standard online card payments
tiers.notes: The US pricing page lists 2.9% + $0.30 per successful domestic-card transaction, with no setup or monthly fee. Country-specific rates can differ.

tiers.name: International card surcharge
tiers.notes: The same US page lists an additional 1.5% for international cards and an additional 1% when currency conversion is required.

tiers.name: ACH Direct Debit
tiers.notes: The US local-methods page lists 0.8% per transaction for standard settlement, capped at $5, with separate failed-payment, dispute, and optional validation fees.

tiers.name: Custom
tiers.notes: Custom pricing is available for high payment volume or unusual business models, including interchange-plus, volume, and multi-product options.

pros: Standard pricing has no setup fee or monthly platform fee for basic payments on the published US page
The pricing page itemizes domestic cards, international-card and currency-conversion surcharges, local payment methods, and custom-pricing options
Payment Links provides a no-code route while APIs support custom payment and billing flows
cons: The 2.9% + $0.30 headline is the US domestic-card rate, not a universal global price
International cards, currency conversion, manually entered cards, disputes, failed payments, and optional products can add separate charges
Billing, fraud tools, tax, identity, issuing, and other Stripe products have their own pricing rather than being included automatically in the base card rate

faq.question: How much does Stripe charge for online card payments?
faq.answer: On Stripe’s US standard pricing page, domestic online card payments are listed at 2.9% + $0.30 per successful transaction. Country-specific pricing can differ.

faq.question: Does Stripe charge a monthly fee for standard payments?
faq.answer: The US standard page says there are no setup fees or monthly fees for the standard payments package. Optional products and usage still have their own charges.

faq.question: What can add to the Stripe card rate?
faq.answer: The US page lists additional charges for manually entered cards, international cards, and currency conversion; disputes, failed payments, alternative methods, and other Stripe products can also have separate fees.
